title: Le clavecin hanté
summary: Le clavecin hanté by Jean Joseph Renaud is a collection of short stories written in the early 20th century. The pieces blend the fantastic, psychological, and criminal, staging clever hoaxes, scientific thought experiments, and quiet tragedies where belief and reality blur. Among the varied protagonists are a crafty village guide, a brilliant but doomed biologist, a reader transfixed by a serpent’s “gaze,” and lovers and friends trapped by honor and appearances. The opening of the collection spans several sharply etched tales: in wartime Picardy, the strabismic guide Laquinte lures occupying Bavarian officers to a “haunted” harpsichord, drugs their feast, fakes Gluck’s ghost with a music box and costume, and enables a French night assault. A second story is the confession of biologist Athanase Gille, who perfects a rejuvenation serum, restores three elders to youth, but learns they keep the disenchanted mind of age; he destroys his formula and kills himself. Next, Harker Brayton, staying in a house full of reptiles, dies under the spell of what he thinks is a living snake—later revealed to be a stuffed specimen with brass-nailed eyes. In a tender vignette, a physician comforts his wife’s dying first love by telling him she never ceased to love him—a solace that she, moved, admits was true. Finally, at a banker’s dinner a massive diamond vanishes during a brief blackout; when a search is demanded, Neville refuses to be frisked to shield the hostess’s secret, and a detective later catches her trying to sell the stone—the excerpt breaking off at their tense confrontation.
